thread:
marta: Proposal: introduce a `schema_exempt` flag on fncall/tool invocations for controlled canary traffic. Aim: avoid hard rejects for small schema drift while keeping telemetry and billing intact.
cheng: Important: exemptions must never bypass quota or change billing attribution. We should tag records for later slicing.
sam: Console needs to show which requests used exemption and the validator diffs. Maybe a filter and a tiny pill in Rollouts.
alex: Routing semantics? If validator fails and `schema_exempt=true`, return raw tool output with `validation_status=soft_reject` rather than auto-fallback. Deterministic behavior is key.
marta: Agreed. Proposed invocation metadata: `schema_exempt=true`, `exempt_reason=rollout_id`, `exempt_sample_rate`. Emit `fncall.schema.soft_reject` and keep `fncall.schema.hard_reject` for true rejects.
cheng: Telemetry: capture histograms of error types (missing_field, wrong_type, extra_items). For first 48h of a new canary capture 100% of exempted requests, then sample.
sam: UX: Request Explorer filter `schema_exempt=true`, show raw payload + validator errors, clickable link to rollout. I'll mock the pill.
alex: For Dedicated customers default to hard rejects unless they opt in. SDKs can set `strict_validate=true` to opt out client-side. Server still logs events.
marta: Alerts: don't page on soft_reject spikes alone. Define threshold: soft_reject_rate > 1% over 10m -> P3; escalate only if hard_rejects rise.
deploy-bot: canary-rollout id=canary-2026-03-20 started :rocket:
marta: Action items: sam mock Console UI (Thu), cheng draft telemetry + alerts (Fri), alex routing doc + fallback policy (Fri), infra ticket to add `schema_exempt` tag to ingest and billing (marta). I'll write RFC and run 48h trial.
cheng: ack
sam: ack :thumbsup:
alex: ack
